3.  Resolutions of the City Council of the City of Avalon Appointing a Director and Alternate
  Director to the California Intergovernmental Risk Authority (CIRA) Board of Directors and
  California Transit Systems Joint Powers Authority (CaITIP)
  The City is a member of the California Intergovernmental Risk Authority (CIRA), and is
  also a member of California Transit Systems (CaITIP). Each CIRA and CaITIP member
  agency appoints a Director and Alternate Director to the Board of Directors. This allows
  each member agency input to direct and control the organization.
  Recommended Action
  1. Adopt resolution authorizing the City Manager to serve as the Director and Assistant
  City Manager to serve as the Alternate Director to the California Intergovernmental Risk
  Authority (C IRA) Board of Directors. 2. Adopt resolution authorizing the Assistant City
  Manager to serve as the Director and City Manager to serve as the Alternate Director to
  the California Transit Systems Joint Powers Authority (CaITIP) Board of Directors.

4.  Appointment of Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference
  and General Assembly Delegate
  The Annual Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and
  General Assembly will be held in Palm Desert, CA from May 2-3, 2024. The City’s
  voting delegate will vote on agenda items pertaining to the General Assembly  —

  Business Meeting.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution appointing Mayor Ann H. Marshall as the City of Avalon voting
  delegate and Councilmember Michael Ponce as the alternate delegate for the Annual
  Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and General
  Assembly in May 2024.

5.  Adopt Ordinance Amending Title 2, Chapter 2-2, Section 2-2.307 City Manager Powers
  and Duties of the Avalon Municipal Code
  This ordinance was introduced and all further readings were waived during the December
  12, 2023 City Council Meeting. The revised ordinance amends Title 2, Chapter 2-2,
  Section 2-2.307 of the Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) to broaden the powers of the City
  Manager to include appointment, removal, promotion and demotion of the office of the
  City Clerk.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Title 2, Chapter 2-2, Section 2-2.307
  City Manager Powers and Duties of the Avalon Municipal Code.

6.  2024 Waterside Permit Renewals
  Waterside Permits expire annually on December 31st If the Harbor Master determines
  that, because of changed circumstances, a permit should not be renewed, or should be
  renewed on different terms and conditions, he shall forward his recommendation thereon
  to the City Council for action, together with a list of all permits that he recommends should
  be renewed for another term without change.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the Harbor Master to renew the attached list of Waterside Permits for 2024.

7.  Resolution Authorizing the City Manager to Execute and File State Documents for
  Approved State Projects and Activities
  The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) requires every agency that
  applies for and/or received funding for approved transportation activities have an
  executed Master Agreement. The Master Agreement establishes rules and regulations
  as well as responsibilities of both local agencies and the State of California regarding the
  utilization of transportation funds. Authority to execute the agreement must be established
  by resolution.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution authorizing the City Manager to execute and file state documents for
  approved transportation projects and activities.

PUBLIC HEARING

8.  Appeal of Planning Commission Action No. 23-26 of PC#2854 Denying a Site Plan and
  a Variance at 335 Wrigley Terrace Road
  On December 6, 2023, the Planning Commission held a duly noticed public hearing to
  consider PC#2854, a request for a Site Plan Review and a Variance to allow a 6-foot tall
  masonry wall within the front yard setback and new gated carport pergolas for two
  autoette parking pads for a single-family residential property at 335 Wrigley Terrance
  Road.
  Recommended Action
  1. Open the Public Hearing. 2. Receive Public Comment. 3. Close the Public Hearing. 4.
  Consider the appeal and determine to either a) Affirm the action of the Planning
  Commission; b) Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other evidence
  upon which the Planning Commission made its decision, and after receiving such
  evidence take such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; c) Refer
  the matter back to the Planning Commission, with or without instructions for further
  proceedings; or d) Set the matter for hearing before itself, considered de novo. (Avalon
  Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.601)

GENERAL BUSINESS

9.  Ratification of Prior Action State of Emergency Proclamation for January 2024 Storm
  —

  Surge Damage
  On January 10, 2024 significant storm surge, exacerbated by king tide conditions and
  high winds, caused damage to the roadway and shoreline public access along Pebbly
  Beach Road near Lover’s Cove. On January 11, 2024, the City Manager, exercising his
  authority as the Director of Emergency Services of the City of Avalon, made a declaration
  of a local state of emergency due infrastructure failures resulting from significant storm
  surge.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution ratifying prior action of the City Manager and making the appropriate
  findings in proclaiming the existence of a local emergency caused by significant storm
  surge on January 10, 2024.

10.  Waterside Project Application Huttopia
  —

  The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application for the use of a 23 foot
  vessel to transport guests between Avalon Harbor and Whites Landing between April
  and November. Huttopia has replaced Mountain & Sea Adventures as lessee &
  operator of White’s Landing. Mountain & Sea Adventures has relinquished their
  Waterside Permit which included two larger vessels.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant a Waterside Project Application to Huttopia, with the following
  conditions: 1. All operations to load and unload passengers will take place on the Pleasure
  Pier floats or Cabrillo Mole floats on a space available basis, except on cruise ship days
  when all loading and unloading will be from the floats on the Pleasure Pier. 2. Applicant
  abides by the Standard List of Conditions for Waterside Permit Holders.

11.  Waterside Project Application Avalon Aquatic Excursions
  —

  The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to offer sightseeing, whale
  and dolphin watching trips, and Snorkeling tours. The applicant proposes to operate 7
  days a week. Float space is generally available on non-cruise ship days; however, on
  cruise ship days the applicant will operate from Catalina Jet Ski Corp End Float.
  Recommended Action
  Make the affirmative finding that conditions set forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have
  been met and grant the Waterside Project Application to Avalon Anglers, with the
  following conditions: 1. All operations to load and unload charter passengers will take
  place on Pleasure Pier floats except on cruise ship days when all loading and unloading
  will be from Jet Ski Corp end float located at the end of the Pleasure Pier. 2. Applicant
  abides by the Standard List of Conditions for Waterside Permit Holders.

12.  Council Chambers Audio Visual System Upgrade
  In 2015, the City Council approved phases 2 & 3 of the Council Chambers AN upgrade.
  This included the installation of a new camera system, and monitoring/control equipment.
  No major updates or improvements have been performed to the A/V system since the
  installation of the new equipment in 2016.
  Recommended Action
  Per the City’s procurement policy, authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute
  an agreement with Key Code Media, Inc. to upgrade the audio visual (AN) system within
  the City Hall Council Chambers for a not to exceed sum of $125,000. This item is
  budgeted in the Information Systems budget account (10135-6611).

13.  Float 4 and 4A Repair and Refurbishment
  In December 2022, the City Council made the determination that a competitive market
  does not exist for the maintenance of the City-owned harbor floats. The City Council
  authorized the City Manager to dispense with competitive purchasing process and
  designated Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified Composites Inc. as vendors meeting
  the Economic Efficiency standard as outlined in the Avalon Municipal Code section 3-
  4.111 (c).

  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with Catalina Boatyard Inc. for
  repair and refurbishment of Cabrillo Mole Floats 4, 4A for a total contract price of $97,312.

14.  Harbor Patrol Boat Volvo D3 Enqine Replacement
  Patrol Boat 1 and 4 are part of a fleet of 7 boats necessary to carry out the day-to-day
  operations of the City. Each Patrol Boat is equipped with a Volvo D3 engine with an hourly
  range from 2200 (1) to 6000 (4) operating hours. Useful life is generally 8000 hours. It is
  anticipated that Patrol Boat 4 will need engine replacement during the summer of 2024
  and Patrol Boat 1 will need engine replacement in 2025.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to approve an expenditure for purchase of two new Volvo
  D3-200A Engine package systems for Patrol Boat 1 and 4.

SUBJECT:  Resolutions of the City Council of the City of Avalon Appointing a
  Director and Alternate Director to the California Intergovernmental Risk
  Authority (C IRA) Board of Directors and California Transit Systems Joint
  Powers Authority (CaITIP)

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Adopt resolution authorizing the City Manager to serve as
the Director and Assistant City Manager to serve as the Alternate Director to the California
Intergovernmental Risk Authority (C IRA) Board of Directors. 2. Adopt resolution authorizing the
Assistant City Manager to serve as the Director and City Manager to serve as the Alternate
Director to the California Transit Systems Joint Powers Authority (CaITIP) Board of Directors.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon (City) is a member of the California Intergovernmental
Risk Authority (CIRA), a statewide risk sharing Joint Powers Authority (JPA) and is also a
member of California Transit Systems Joint Powers Authority (CaITIP). CIRA exists for the
purpose of providing its member agencies with comprehensive general liability coverage,
workers’ compensation, property insurance, special events insurance, and fidelity bonds. All
members participate in pro-active safety and loss control programs, with the common goals of
reducing risks, minimizing losses, and controlling costs. CaITIP provides similar benefits to the
City, but only for public transportation liability, which is excluded by CIRA.

Each CIRA and CaITIP member agency appoints a Director and Alternate Director to the Board
of Directors. This allows each member agency input to direct and control the organization. The
Members work toward common goals and objectives to minimize loss exposures, expand
coverage, and, ultimately, reduce costs. The Finance Director currently serves as the Alternate
Director to the CIRA and Director to the CaITIP Board of Directors. The City Manager currently
serves as the Director to the CIRA and Alternate Director to the CaITIP Board of Directors.

Staff recommends continuing with the City Manager as the Director to the CIRA Board of
Directors, with the Assistant City Manager appointed as the Alternate Director.

Additionally, Staff recommends the Assistant City Manager be named as the Director to the
CaITIP Board of Directors with the City Manager to remain as the Alternate Director.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.
 CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The Finance Director
would remain identified as the Director and Alternate member of the CaITIP/CIRA Board of
Directors.

SUBJECT:  Adopt Ordinance Amending Title 2, Chapter 2-2, Section 2-2.307
  City Manager Powers and Duties of the Avalon Municipal Code

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Title 2,
Chapter 2-2, Section 2-2.307 City Manager Powers and Duties of the Avalon Municipal Code.

REPORT SUMMARY: This ordinance was introduced and all further readings were waived
during the December 12, 2023 City Council Meeting.

City Staff recommend amending Title 2, Chapter 2-2, Section 2-2.307 of the Avalon Municipal
Code (AMC) to broaden the powers of the City Manager to include appointment, removal,
promotion and demotion of the office of the City Clerk.

As written, the AMC exempts the office of the City Clerk as the position is appointed by resolution
of the City Council. City Staff recommend reorganizing the structure of the office of the City Clerk
to have the office report directly to the City Manager rather than the City Council. With this
proposed amendment the City Manager will provide oversight of the City Clerk’s Office.

The office of the City Clerk is administrative in nature with the City Clerk providing oversight of
public records requests, compliance with various governmental regulations, including annual
reporting to the FPPC and citywide records management. The City Clerk also acts as the local
elections official.

In recent history, the City Clerk position has been a dual title held in conjunction with the City
Manager or Chief Administrative Officer. At this time, the City does not have a permanent and
dedicated City Clerk. Duties of the City Clerk Office are shared divided between a Deputy City
Clerk/Senior Administrative Assistant and Management Analyst.

Additionally, Staff are taking this opportunity to further amend the ordinance to make it gender
neutral when referencing the City Manager.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The Avalon Municipal
Code will not be amended.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Publication pursuant to state law requirements.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

REPORT SUMMARY: On December 6, 2023, the Planning Commission held a duly
noticed public hearing to consider PC#2854, a request for a Site Plan Review and a
Variance to allow a 6-foot tall masonry wall within the front yard setback and new gated
carport pergolas for two autoette parking pads for a single-family residential property at
335 Wrigley Terrance Road (Wrigley Drive). The property is located in the Multiple Family,
Medium Density (MD) zone. The property owner, Eric Albert, was represented by Fineline
Construction, Inc. The staff report and meeting minutes are included as Attachments 1
and 2 of this report.
Variances were requested because the proposed project does not comply with
development standards set forth in Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) as follows:

  •  Per AMC Section 9-7.801 a, fences and walls shall not exceed a height of 42
  inches within the required front yard setback. The proposed wall and retractable
  carport gates are 6-foot in height.

  •  Per AMC Section 9-7.404.b.8, no structure or part of a structure not specified
  above may project into required setbacks without the granting of a variance. The
  proposed carport pergolas are located within the front setback area of the property.

In the opinion of staff, the findings for a Variance could not be made for the additional
height in the front setback area for the following reasons:

  •  The configuration of site development, while unique to the property, does not
  prevent the applicant from complying with the intent of the zoning regulations for
   wall and gate height. The existing front property wall is shorter than permitted by
  code. The applicant did not adequately consider other options to secure the
  property that would either not require a variance, require a lesser variance, and/or
  would have less of an impact the scenic view of Avalon Bay from Wrigley Terrace
  Road. Options discussed with the applicant by staff included:

  o  Building a shorter wall;
  o  Proposing a wall/fence/gate design that would be see through, such as
  pickets or wrought iron; or
  o  Including defensible features only in areas where trespassing is a concern,
  such as where the roofline connects to the retaining wall.

  Therefore, the applicant had created a self-imposed hardship by not modifying the
  design of their project to more closely comply with municipal code development
  standards, and a Variance could not be justified for the project in its current form.

  •  Two of the policies of the City’s General Plan/Local Coastal Plan are to strengthen
  the visual and physical connection between the waterfront and neighborhoods
  surrounding Avalon Bay (Policy 11-2) and to incorporate policies of the Coastal Act
  as guiding policies of the City’s land use, which includes protection of scenic
  coastal vistas (Policy 11-3). Wrigley Terrace Road is a public right-of-way and is
  established as a scenic corridor regularly enjoyed by residents and visitors. As
  there are multiple design options that could be considered by the applicant that
  would better preserve the views from the public right-of-way and still achieve the
  goal of securing the property, the proposed project is in conflict with Geneal Plan
  policies and could not meet the findings for granting a Variance.

  •  Construction of a solid 6-foot wall at the front property line along Wrigley Terrace
  Road would create an enclosed tunnel effect between property and adjacent
  retaining wall on the other side of road which is not in keeping with the development
  pattern in the “Terraces” neighborhood. The other residence on this section of
  Wrigley Terrace Road have set back their front yard fence from the front property
  line, reducing the imposition of the vertical mass at the street. Therefore, there is
  no existing precedent to approve a solid 6-foot tall wall at the property line.

It was the opinion of staff that a Variance could be granted for the proposed carport
pergolas due to their less visually intrusive design. However, given that the carport
pergolas are part of the overall project with the wall and retracting gates, staff could not
recommend approval of this portion of the project.

After consideration of the findings in the staff report, applicant presentation, and public
comment, the Planning Commission voted 5-0 to adopt PC Resolution 23-26 and deny
the project as presented at the public hearing (Attachment 3).

On December 13, 2023, Adrian Thoricht of Fineline Construction, Inc. filed a timely appeal
of the Planning Commission’s decision, requesting that the City Council hear the Project
 de novo at a public hearing and consider two alternative wall designs that address the
findings made in the staff report and feedback provided by Commissioners during the
public hearing (Attachment 4).
Pursuant to AMC Section 9-8.601 .B, upon receiving notice of an appeal, the City Council
may take any of the following actions:
  1. Affirm the action of the Commission; or
  2. Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other evidence upon
  which the Commission made its decision, and after receiving such evidence take
  such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; or
  3. Refer the matter back to the Commission, with or without instructions for further

  4. Set the matter for hearing before itself. At such hearing, it shall hear and decide
  the case de novo.

Staff supports the Planning Commission’s denial of the Project as presented at the
December 6, 2023 public hearing, as discussed above. However, in the appeal
application the applicant has demonstrated a willingness to modify their design to address
the deficiencies identified in the findings for denial of the Variance. Therefore, it is the
opinion of staff that there are grounds for further consideration of the project by City
Council or the Planning Commission.

Dear Kelly;

The subject property, 335 Wrigley Terrace Road in Avalon, is a steep parcel (36-degree slope) that is
bordered on the south by Wrigley Terrace Road and the north by Upper Terrace Road. There is one
neighboring residence to the west, 333 Wrigley, whereas the easterly property is an unimproved lot.

335 Wrigley is a large single-family residence with a pool and landscaping on a large lot (5 combined
smaller lots). The residence is consistent with other properties in the area.

When the new owner, Eric Albert, recently purchased the property, he noticed that tourists frequently
park their golf carts in front his residence and take photos, sometimes walking onto each of his carport
decks. The area in front of his place is on the end of a blind curve, which is vulnerable to the tour buses
and large trucks that traverse Wrigley when Pebbly Beach Road is closed.

At the length of his property bordering Wrigley Terrace Road, there is a white stucco wall that sits
entirely on his lot, varying 23-33” in height; this is not sufficient to keep people from standing or sitting
on the wall. This is of particular concern in that the ground level on his property is over 11’ below the
wall and a fall from that height could be very serious at best. Additionally, the short wall height
enables people to climb onto it and then onto his roof, causing damage and exposing him to further
liability. To mitigate these liabilities and public safety issues, the owner would like to raise the wall to 6’
in height. This would eliminate the fall risks and stop people from being able to access his roof. Because
the house itself and its adjoining landscape walls are stucco, the proposed increase of height should be
stuccoed to match.

Although the proposed 6’ wall would in no way block the view of any of the residents, concerns have
been raised that it blocks the view for the tourists, to that end, we propose placing holes through the
wall that photos can be taken through but are not large enough to crawl through. By this compromise,
the threat to public safety and potential liability to the owner are both mitigated.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): City Council make the affirmative finding that conditions set
forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have been met and grant a Waterside Project Application to
Huttopia, with the following conditions:

  1. All operations to load and unload passengers will take place on the Pleasure Pier floats
  or Cabrillo Mole floats on a space available basis, except on cruise ship days when all
  loading and unloading will be from the floats on the Pleasure Pier.

  2. Applicant abides by the Standard List of Conditions for Waterside Permit Holders.

REPORT SUMMARY: The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application for the use
of a 23 foot vessel to transport guests between Avalon Harbor and Whites Landing between
April and November. Huttopia does not expect to run more than two trips per day and will not be
moored in Avalon overnight. Huttopia personnel will make on-call docking arrangements by
contacting Harbor Patrol on VHF Channel 12, prior to their arrival. Huttopia has replaced
Mountain & Sea Adventures as lessee & operator of White’s Landing. Mountain & Sea
Adventures has relinquished their Waterside Permit which included two larger vessels.

In my opinion as Avalon Harbor Master, this project will not result in any additional boat trips, or
have substantial negative impact on facilities or harbor services, except as noted in subsection
(2), below and the findings required by the Municipal Code can be made.

Section 10-2.416 of the Municipal Code provides that a waterside permit may only be granted
where the City Council is able to make the following affirmative findings:

  (1)  The project will not result in a substantial alteration of the City’s present or planned
waterside uses of the A valon Harbor,
  (2)  With regard to transportation and circulation, the project (i) will not generate
substantial additional boat trips, including shoreboat trips, or other movement within Avalon
Harbor; (ii) will not have a substantial negative impact upon existing mooring, docking, or other
anchorage facilities; (iii) will not have a substantial impact on other modes and systems of
transportation; (iv) will not result in substantial alterations of present patterns of circulation or
movement of people and/or goods; (v) will not increase traffic hazards to swimmers, boaters, or
other existing activities; and (vi) will not restrict or alter existing coastal access;
 Impact: The Pleasure Pier floats see heavy usage in the summer months by rental kayaks, pedal
boats, small rental motor boats along with personal dinghies and pleasure boat traffic.

Mitigation: Huttopia’s use of City floats is on-call only and they will be required to contact the
Harbor Office for docking arrangements upon arrival. Additionally, the Mole floats will be
available on non-cruise ship days.

alteration of existing sources or systems for power, natural gas, communications, water, sewage

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): City Council make the affirmative finding that conditions set
forth in the Avalon Municipal Code have been met and grant the Waterside Project Application
to Avalon Anglers, with the following conditions:

  1. All operations to load and unload charter passengers will take place on Pleasure Pier
  floats except on cruise ship days when all loading and unloading will be from Jet Ski
  Corp end float located at the end of the Pleasure Pier.

  2. Applicant abides by the Standard List of Conditions for Waterside Permit Holders.

REPORT SUMMARY: The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to offer
sightseeing, whale and dolphin watching trips, and Snorkeling tours.

Avalon Aquatic Excursions proposes the use of a 26’ boat to conduct 6 Pack Coastal whale
and dolphin watching trips, and Snorkeling tours in the Avalon area. Avalon Aquatic
Excursions proposes to operate 7 days a week, and on Cruise Ship days from January 1, to
December 31, and between the hours of 8:00 am. to 8:00 p.m. The vessel will obtain a
mooring from Avalon Harbor Patrol as needed. Float space is generally available on non-
cruise ship days however on cruise ship days Avalon Aquatic Excursions will operate from
Catalina Jet Ski Corp End Float located at the end of the Pleasure Pier. When the end float is
removed during from October 16th to May l5” each year, Avalon Aquatic Excursions will not
operate on cruise ship days.

In my opinion as Avalon Harbor Master, the project will not result in any substantial negative
impact upon Avalon Harbor floats, except as noted in subsection (2), below.

Section 10-2.416 of the Municipal Code provides that a waterside permit may only be granted
where the City Council is able to make the following affirmative findings:
  (1)  The project will not result in a substantial alteration of the City’s present or
planned waterside uses of the Avalon Harbor;
  (2)  With regard to transportation and circulation, the project (i) will not generate
substantial additional boat trips, including shoreboat trips, or other movement within Avalon
Harbor; (ii) will not have a substantial negative impact upon existing mooring, docking, or
other anchorage facilities; (iii) will not have a substantial impact on other modes and systems
 of transportation; (iv) will not result in substantial alterations of present patterns of circulation or
movement of people and for goods; (v) will not increase traffic hazards to swimmers, boaters,
or other existing activities; and (vi) will not restrict or alter existing coastal access;

Impact: The Pleasure Pier floats see heavy usage in the summer months by rental kayaks,
pedal boats, small rental motor boats along with personal dinghies and pleasure boat traffic.

Mitigation: Avalon Aquatic Excursions’ use of City floats is on-call only and they will be
required to contact the Harbor Office for docking arrangements upon arrival. Additionally, the
Mole floats will be available on non-cruise ship days.

  (3)  The project will not have a substantial impact upon, and will not result in, a need
for new or altered governmental services, including but not limited to fire, police, maintenance
of facilities, and harbor department services;
  (4)  The project will not result in the use of substantial amounts of fuel or other forms
of energy or substantially increase the demand upon existing energy or require the
development of new sources of energy;
  (5)  The project will not result in the need for new utility systems or a substantial
alteration of existing sources or systems for power, natural gas, communications, water,
sewage disposal or solid waste;
  (6)  The project will not obstruct any scenic vista or view open to the public, and will
not result in the creation of an aesthetically offensive site which is open to public view;
  (7)  The project will not result in a substantial negative impact upon the quality and
quantity of existing recreational opportunities or result in alterations or restrictions to coastal
access;
  (8)  The applicant is fit to be entrusted with the privileges of a permit, in that he has
not engaged in prior violations of the City’s harbor regulations, including the provisions of this
article, has timely paid any harbor-related fees and has not presented checks returned for
insufficient funds.

The Municipal Code also provides that the “City Council may deny the permit where the
impacts listed in paragraphs (1) through (8) above are cumulatively significant, even though
the individual impacts are limited. The City Council may approve a project where mitigation
measures eliminating significant impacts are incorporated into the project, and the approval
shall be conditioned upon the implementation of such mitigation measures. The failure to
comply and maintain any mitigation measures shall be a basis for suspension or revocation of
a waterside permit.”

SUBJECT:  Council Chambers Audio Visual System Upgrade

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Per the City’s procurement policy, authorize the City Manager,
or designee, to execute an agreement with Key Code Media, Inc. to upgrade the audio visual
(AN) system within the City Hall Council Chambers for a not to exceed sum of $125,000. This
item is budgeted in the Information Systems budget account (10135-6611).

REPORT SUMMARY: In November 2015, the City Council approved phases 2 & 3 of the Council
Chambers A/V upgrade. This included the installation of a new camera system, and
monitoring/control equipment. No major updates or improvements have been performed to the
AJV system since the installation of the new equipment in 2016. The existing equipment is quickly
becoming outdated, and several issues continuously need to be addressed. These issues mainly
include videoconferencing (Zoom, MS Teams, etc.) problems, feedback/interference, online
audio not working, and difficulty of use due to the complexity of the system.

Staff reached out to three audio visual companies to review our existing system, and each
company created a proposal for a solution that would work for our Council Chambers AN needs.
The proposed equipment upgrade would make use of the existing camera system and wiring,
which reduced the overall cost. It involves replacing most of the outdated audio monitoring &
control components, along with the installation of new microphones & monitors at the dais. The
new system would be much more user friendly, allow for remote user accessibility, includes a
voting system, would have full technical support, and will create a much more improved &
professional viewing experience.

The three companies that staff worked with were Key Code Media Inc., Western Audio Visual &
Security, and Spinitar Solutionz. We asked all three companies to provide similar solutions, and
the proposal from Key Code Media ended up at the lowest cost totaling $123,703.13. This is a
maximum amount proposed, and the cost will likely be less as time & materials would be billed
at actual cost. Obtaining three proposals fulfilled the informal bid competitive process purchasing
procedure requirement specified in the Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.106(a).

made the determination that a competitive market does not exist for the maintenance of the
City-owned harbor floats. The City Council authorized the City Manager to dispense with
competitive purchasing process and designated Catalina Boatyard Inc. and Diversified
Composites Inc. as vendors meeting the Economic Efficiency standard as outlined in the
Avalon Municipal Code section 3-4.111(c).

Mole Floats 4, 4A are integral to the Cabrillo Mole Transportation Terminal and part of a
necessary dock system that allows for the loading and unloading of passengers and freight to
Avalon Harbor. Each float system consist of two attached docks designated as 4, 4A and 5,
5A. Floats 4, 4A are overdue for repair and refurbishment.

While floats 1-3 are of a steel and composite build materials, floats 4, 4A and 5, 5A are
constructed of plywood and fiberglass materials. Per the City’s finding of economic efficiency,
the Harbor Master contacted Dennis Choate of Diversified Composites in Long Beach and
Caleb Lins of Catalina Boatyard Inc. for bids on rehabilitating Floats 4, 4A.

Per the terms of the procurement policy, the contract award must be brought to the City
Council for approval.

Only one vendor Catalina Boatyard Inc.
  —  — provided a proposal. Per the proposal, Catalina
Boatyard Inc. agreed to perform the following scope of work for a total contract price of
$97,312.00:
  • Haul out and launch of each float
  • High Pressure Power wash of bottom sides and deck
  • Prep and apply anti fouling bottom paint
  • Replace sacrificial plywood wear sheathing on both sides
  • Fix or replace non-skid worn areas
  • Apply epoxy paint to deck sides
 As a part of the proposal, Catalina Boatyard, Inc. agreed to furnish the following materials:
  • All needed abrasives
  • PPE
  • Antifouling paints
  • Epoxy paints
  • Marine grade plywood
  • 5200 Adhesives
  • All necessary fasteners

Staff recommend authorizing the City Manager to enter into an agreement with Catalina
Boatyard Inc. for repair and refurbishment of floats 4, 4A.
